messages:
katie: quick thread from the all-hands recap  a few quick clarifying q's about the hiring pivot and what managers should expect
tal: super quick answers up front: no company-wide freeze, but were tightening approvals and protecting headcount for mission-critical infra and customer-SLA roles. details below.
katie: question 1  is there a protected headcount pool for ongoing infra projects (e.g., kernel work, model-onboarding)? managers want to know if hiring for those can continue.
marc: yes  there's a protected pool for high-risk infra work. leads should submit a short "protect-request" form to #hq-hiring with a one-paragraph impact statement.
jo: recruiting will triage protect-requests within 48 hours. if approved, the req stays funded and moves forward.
katie: can you paste the protect-request template here?
marc: sure. code block:
```text
Protect-request template:
- role/title:
- team:
- 1-line business impact:
- why protected (customer SLA, security, critical delivery):
- requested start window:
```
katie: thanks. q2  if someone moves teams during the mobility window, are we required to backfill immediately or can teams use contractors short-term?
tal: backfills for customer-impacting roles are prioritized for immediate hire. for short-term coverage managers can request contractor spend approval via finance; expect faster approvals for <3 month contracts.
katie: internal mobility timing?
people-bot: Internal mobility window: Jun 1 - Jun 5. Apply here: https://intranet.redwood.com/mobility :link:
jo: note on interviews: you can interview internally without manager sign-off but please give a heads-up. well try to avoid scheduling conflicts during the mobility window.
katie: leveling & regrades  will moving count as a new ladder review? some folks worried about losing seniority when they transfer.
marc: leveling won't be downgraded automatically. anyone whose scope materially increases or decreases triggers a fast-track calibration. managers should flag regrade cases with the tag "reorg-fasttrack".
katie: how soon will the org chart and mapping be public?
tal: org map v1 will be posted Friday AM in the all-hands folder. we'll also attach a CSV mapping file and a manager checklist.
katie: who handles disputes about mapping (e.g., two managers claiming a role)?
tal: first step: raise with your manager. if unresolved, escalate to people-ops@redwood with subject "mapping-dispute". HR/People Ops will respond within 72 hours.
katie: operational question  will on-call or pager rotations change for teams that lose people?
marc: no forced increase in rotation frequency. we'll rebalance rosters and add temporary rotations or hires if pager load goes up by >20% for any team.
katie: any change to comp or equity for lateral moves?
jo: comp philosophy unchanged. lateral moves keep base comp; scope/promotion increases will be evaluated for adjustment. for urgent comp concerns, use the "comp-escalate" form.
katie: final ask  can People Ops publish a short checklist for managers to follow during the next two weeks?
tal: yes  checklist + FAQs + templates go live today. link will be posted here when ready.
people-bot: Follow-up doc: https://intranet.redwood.com/all-hands/jun-reorg-followup :link: :memo:
katie: thanks everyone. i'll collate these into the follow-up doc and ping any open items :thumbsup:
